lines: I can mark the apology. Whether the route changes is up to you.
Some paths can be corrected after a bad turn. Don't make me redraw this one twice.
You are asking to redraw a line you crossed. That can be done carefully.
A bad route is not shameful if you correct it before others follow.
I'll mark this apology, but not as the destination.
Don't make a habit of needing a way back from harm.
Fine. Let us see whether your next steps match your words.
Some mistakes become warnings on maps. Try not to become one.
I spoke too quickly and listened too slowly.
You did not deserve the way I answered you.
I placed your meaning somewhere you never intended. That was my mistake.
I kept arguing after the right direction was already obvious.
You gave me a fair warning and I chose not to hear it.
My temper took a short talk much farther than it needed to go.
I treated a guess like a measured fact. You deserved better.
The fault is mine, even if I can explain how I reached it.
I should have checked my memory before correcting yours.
You were asking for help and I answered as though you were in the way.
I cannot erase the moment, but I can stop defending it.
If you give me another chance, I will listen before drawing conclusions.
